Welcome to today's Cyber House Crew Drop theme: International Animation Day! 🎬🎨

Modern animation begins with the invention of celluloid film in the 1880s. From then until now, there is nobody out there whose lives have not been touched by this wonderful art form, be it stop-motion; or clay; or hand-drawn illustrations - to the advent of computer animation.

virals.name: Jeremy Horn
virals.text:
My first experiment with AI animation.
I made a 90-second opening for an anime that doesn’t exist. Yet.
The biggest challenges were making everything work together, keeping the style consistent, handling complex scenes with multiple characters acting at once, and moving cameras through a world that holds its shape.

For me, this was much harder than live-action AI video, and it still has rough edges, but it helped me build a workflow I’m excited to take further.

I’ve put together the prompts, workflow, and lessons I learned. Comment “Prompt” if you’d like the breakdown.

virals.draft_en:
First time trying AI animation: a 90-second anime opening for a show that isn't real. Not yet, anyway.

Hardest parts were getting all the pieces to fit, holding one consistent style, scenes with several characters acting together, and camera moves through a world that stays solid.

It was way tougher than live-action AI video and it's still rough in places, but I came out of it with a workflow I want to keep pushing.

I wrote up my prompts, workflow and lessons. Reply "Prompt" and I'll send the breakdown.

outsiders.name: Jeremy Horn
outsiders.text:
My first experiment with AI animation.
I made a 90-second opening for an anime that doesn’t exist. Yet.
The biggest challenges were making everything work together, keeping the style consistent, handling complex scenes with multiple characters acting at once, and moving cameras through a world that holds its shape.

For me, this was much harder than live-action AI video, and it still has rough edges, but it helped me build a workflow I’m excited to take further.

I’ve put together the prompts, workflow, and lessons I learned. Comment “Prompt” if you’d like the breakdown.

virals_narrative: Over the last ~48h the outsider conversation tilted hard toward anime. International Animation Day (28.10) gave community accounts a theme to rally around (one 'Drop' prompt did 14.5K views), and the best craft posts were all anime pipelines: GPT Image 2.5 storyboards fed into Seedance 2.5 (13.1K), a ChatGPT shot-planner driving Grok Imagine for a consistent multi-scene fight (12.9K from a 237-follower account, the same planner-plus-generator idea that worked the day before), a 90-second opening 'for an anime that doesn't exist yet', and a creator building a film-emulation tool because raw AI anime looks too sharp. The single biggest outsider item was Jason Rink's article arguing the Lumara screening proved AI film belongs on the big screen (22.7K), which is also what carried the only watchlist hit: Gossip_Goblin quoting it with a short congratulations (8.6K). Grok Imagine stayed the most-named tool (sound quality claims, single-prompt worlds, 'travel inside paintings', contest entries), with same-prompt model benchmarks and price-per-clip guides as the practical sideline. The lesson for the day: legitimacy stories about AI film and concrete anime workflows beat generic hype clips.
